title: Gender of nouns
summary: Every French noun is masculine or feminine, so learn each one with its article: le livre, la table, un parc, une gare.
With l' and les you cannot hear the gender, so note it when you learn the word: l'hôtel (m), l'école (f).
Endings that are usually masculine: -age, -ment, -eau, -isme, -oir, -ier: le voyage, le bâtiment, le gâteau, le tourisme, le couloir, le quartier.
Endings that are usually feminine: -tion, -sion, -té, -ure, -ie, -ette, -ence, -ée: la natation, la télévision, la santé, la voiture, la boulangerie, la journée.
Learn the common exceptions: la plage, la page, l'image (f), l'eau (f), la peau, le musée, le lycée, le silence.
Days, months, seasons and languages are masculine: le lundi, le printemps, l'été (m), le français.
Some nouns change meaning with gender: le tour (a trip round) / la tour (a tower), le livre (a book) / la livre (a pound), le poste (a job) / la poste (the post office).
Many job nouns have a feminine form: un infirmier → une infirmière, un vendeur → une vendeuse, un acteur → une actrice, un musicien → une musicienne.
Job nouns that already end in -e are the same for both: un journaliste / une journaliste, un dentiste / une dentiste.

cards.front: Why should you always learn a French noun with le/la or un/une?
cards.back: Gender changes the article, the adjectives and the pronouns, and you usually can't work it out from the meaning: le livre (m), la table (f). With l' and les the gender is hidden, so note it: l'hôtel (m), l'école (f).

cards.front: Name six noun endings that are usually masculine.
cards.back: -age (le fromage), -ment (le bâtiment), -eau (le bateau), -isme (le tourisme), -oir (le couloir), -ier (le quartier).

cards.front: Name six noun endings that are usually feminine.
cards.back: -tion/-sion (la natation, la télévision), -té (la santé), -ure (la voiture), -ie (la boulangerie), -ette (la baguette), -ence (la différence). Most nouns in -ée are feminine too: la journée, l'idée.

cards.prompt: Le matin, mon père va à ___ boulangerie pour acheter des croissants.
cards.en: In the morning my father goes to the baker's to buy croissants.
cards.why: -ie is a feminine ending: la boulangerie, la pharmacie, la géographie.

cards.prompt: Pour mon anniversaire, ma grand-mère a fait ___ gâteau au chocolat.
cards.en: For my birthday my grandmother made a chocolate cake.
cards.why: -eau is a masculine ending: un gâteau, un bateau, un cadeau.

cards.front: Which common nouns break the ending rules?
cards.back: Feminine although they end in -age: la plage, la page, l'image. Masculine although they end in -ée: le musée, le lycée. Masculine although it ends in -ence: le silence. Feminine although they end in -eau: l'eau, la peau.

cards.prompt: Il y a ___ plage magnifique près de notre hôtel.
cards.en: There is a magnificent beach near our hotel.
cards.why: plage is feminine, an exception to the masculine -age ending (like la page and l'image).

cards.prompt: Demain, nous allons visiter ___ musée des sciences.
cards.en: Tomorrow we are going to visit the science museum.
cards.why: Most nouns in -ée are feminine, but musée (like lycée) is masculine.

cards.front: What do these pairs mean: le tour / la tour, le livre / la livre, le poste / la poste, le mode / la mode?
cards.back: le tour = a tour, a trip round; la tour = a tower. le livre = a book; la livre = a pound (money, or 500 g). le poste = a job, a position or a (TV) set; la poste = the post office. le mode = a method, a way; la mode = fashion.

cards.prompt: Du haut de ___ tour, on voit toute la ville.
cards.en: From the top of the tower you can see the whole town.
cards.why: la tour = a tower; le tour = a tour or a trip round something.

cards.prompt: Ce week-end, on va faire ___ tour du lac à vélo.
cards.en: This weekend we're going to cycle round the lake.
cards.why: le tour = a trip round something (faire le tour de); la tour = a tower.

cards.prompt: Pour envoyer ce colis, il faut aller à ___ poste.
cards.en: To send this parcel you have to go to the post office.
cards.why: la poste = the post office; le poste = a job or position.

cards.front: How do job nouns change to refer to a woman?
cards.back: Often just add -e: un avocat → une avocate. Also -ier/-er → -ière/-ère (infirmière, boulangère), -ien → -ienne (musicienne), -eur → -euse (vendeuse, chanteuse), -teur → -trice (actrice, directrice). Nouns already ending in -e don't change: un/une journaliste, un/une secrétaire.

cards.prompt: Ma tante travaille comme ___ dans un hôpital à Lyon.
cards.en: My aunt works as a nurse in a hospital in Lyon.
cards.why: -ier becomes -ière for a woman, with a grave accent: une infirmière.

cards.en: Later on, Chloé would like to become an actress.
cards.why: Most job nouns in -teur become -trice for a woman: un acteur → une actrice. No article is needed after devenir or être with a job.

cards.prompt: Ma sœur rêve de devenir ___ dans un groupe de rock.
cards.en: My sister dreams of becoming a singer in a rock band.
cards.why: chanteur comes from the verb chanter, so it follows the -eur → -euse pattern (like vendeur → vendeuse), not -teur → -trice.

cards.prompt: Ma mère est ___ pour une chaîne de télévision.
cards.en: My mother is a journalist for a TV channel.
cards.why: Nouns ending in -e (journaliste, dentiste, secrétaire, élève) are the same for both genders; only the article shows it: une journaliste.

cards.instruction: Rewrite the sentence so it is about a female cousin, changing the words in bold.
cards.why: cousin → cousine, so mon → ma; -ien doubles the n and adds -e: musicienne.
